claims.text: An ML framework using detailed phonon descriptors can predict low lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys more accurately than traditional DFT-based or simplified scattering models.
FeCoCrMnNi is a multicomponent random high-entropy alloy with inherent atomic disorder.
The target FeCoCrMnNi-like alloys are single-phase.
The target alloys exhibit significant mass and force-constant fluctuations.
Phonon density of states, phonon lifetimes, and force-constant-disorder metrics contain information relevant to lattice thermal conductivity.
A model trained on combined computed vibrational data and experimental inelastic-scattering measurements will improve predictive performance.
Machine-learned force fields trained using ab initio molecular-dynamics data have been used with Green–Kubo methods to predict thermal conductivity.
Force-constant fluctuations associated with atomic disorder enhance phonon attenuation or scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Disorder-enhanced phonon scattering reduces phonon lifetimes.
Enhanced phonon scattering and reduced phonon lifetimes lower lattice thermal conductivity.
Encoding detailed vibrational properties allows the ML model to capture disorder-induced phonon scattering.
Traditional DFT-based approaches often oversimplify configurational disorder and force-constant fluctuations in high-entropy alloys.
Phonon transport is the dominant heat-conduction mechanism in the target high-entropy alloys from approximately 300 to 700 K.
The target alloys remain disordered and single-phase throughout approximately 300–700 K.
The ML framework will reduce prediction error by at least 20% relative to current DFT-based or simplified models.
The ML framework will reliably identify high-entropy alloys having lattice thermal conductivity below 1 W/(m·K).
The approach will be unreliable for phase-separated alloys, disorder regimes absent from the training data, or regimes with important electronic heat conduction.
